quests.title: {PLANET}
quests.allDone: Nine seams, nine worlds. Hope has the wire and Meru has the door. Whatever happens next happens somewhere else.

steps.text: Find your feet in {PLANET} TOWN SQUARE
Ask about the GLOW-WORM GROTTO — HOPE at the CASTLE, or BRAM at the SKI LODGE
why: Two keepers have worked that cave on their own for forty years, and the thing living in it stopped being a job a long time ago.

steps.text: Go down to the GLOW-WORM GROTTO and talk to WREN

why: Wren deflects. Barrow is the one who will admit he does not go over any more — and he is the one holding the feed pail.

steps.text: Buy the KEEPER'S DRAUGHT at the ITEM SHOP
why: Fenn has stocked them out of habit for thirty years. Bait he trusts, a draught in it, and the undercut floor he has been lying on does the rest.

steps.text: Settle the thing in the GROTTO

why: Forty years at that wall and he never once took it out. He will now.

steps.text: Take the SEAM STONE NORTH to HOPE, at the CASTLE
why: Nine mounts and one stone in it. Hope is the only one on this planet who has been reading.

gayaChurch.label: Clubhouse 8
gayaChurch.note: Your clubhouse. Eight machines, one counter, and the sign is yours to write.
gayaChurch.name: The Clubhouse

gayaMountainPath.note: {PLANET} Ski Lodge. Rentals by the shed, fire in the middle, chair at the top of the plaza.
gayaMountainPath.intro: {PLANET} Ski Lodge. Rentals by the shed, fire in the middle, chair at the top of the plaza.
gayaMountainPath.name: {PLANET} Ski Lodge

gayaMountainBase.label: Mount {PLANET} Slopes
gayaMountainBase.note: Mount {PLANET}. Three runs, gates set, chair running. Something has been building snowmen.
gayaMountainBase.intro: Mount {PLANET}. Three runs, gates set, chair running. Something has been building snowmen.
gayaMountainBase.name: Mount {PLANET} Slopes

gayaMountainCave.note: The Glow-Worm Grotto. Two keepers, forty years of feeding, and it shows.
gayaMountainCave.intro: The Glow-Worm Grotto. Two keepers, forty years of feeding, and it shows.
gayaMountainCave.name: The Glow-Worm Grotto

gayaCanyon.intro: {PLANET} Lake. Still water, a long jetty, and somebody is always fishing.

gayaSnowFort.label: The Snow Fort
gayaSnowFort.note: The Snow Fort. One way in, the same way out, and it is holding the whole trench.
gayaSnowFort.intro: The Snow Fort. One way in, the same way out, and it is holding the whole trench.
gayaSnowFort.name: The Snow Fort

gayaGlass.note: THE GLASS. The transport was interrupted here. Hold the ground and it will finish the crossing.
gayaGlass.intro: BATTLE. Machines and raiders are coming for the core. Hold it through three waves: fight them off, use the cover, and take out the turrets.
gayaGlass.name: The Glass

gayaApartment.label: Your Apartment
gayaApartment.note: YOUR PLACE. A bed, a table, and a shelf with one space on it.
gayaApartment.name: Your Apartment

npcs.name: Fenn
npcs.greeting: Welcome in. Everything on the shelf is honest stock.
npcs.bio: Keeps the shop on the south wing. Buys nothing, sells everything, and will tell you which of it you actually need.

npcs.name: Bree
npcs.greeting: Steel and plate. Tell me what you need.
npcs.bio: Beats plate in the armory across the avenue. Deaf in one ear and entirely unbothered about it.

npcs.name: Sorrel
npcs.greeting: Sit where you like. Kitchen's still warm.
npcs.bio: Runs the tavern. Has heard every story on this square twice and improves them on the retelling.

npcs.name: Ember-in-Ash
npcs.greeting: Sit. The kettle is for whoever reaches it.
npcs.bio: Acolyte of the Church of {PLANET}. Past the novitiate. Trusted with a shrine of their own.

npcs.name: Fathom
npcs.greeting: It has no bottom that anyone has found. That is the lesson.
npcs.bio: Reader of the Church of {PLANET}. Reads at the rites and keeps the copying honest.

npcs.name: Sounding
npcs.greeting: Put your eyes to the glass. Everyone should see it once.
npcs.bio: Acolyte of the Church of {PLANET}. Past the novitiate. Trusted with a shrine of their own.

npcs.name: Bastion
npcs.greeting: The gate guards watch the road. I watch the shrine.
npcs.bio: Acolyte of the Church of {PLANET}. Past the novitiate. Trusted with a shrine of their own.

npcs.name: Pennant
npcs.greeting: Even a match wants a blessing. Most of them need one.
npcs.bio: Novice of the Church of {PLANET}. Newly of the order. Still gets the early bells.

npcs.name: Grant

lines.text: You seem very calm tonight, Grant.
Why should I not be? {PLANET}'s fleet is average. Our shields are standard. Our weapons are precisely balanced.
Not the strongest, not the weakest. The middle is comfortable.
Why is {PLANET} so suspicious of Meru?
Because nothing should be perfectly central. Meru holds the sun, the broken gate, and the network.
One person holds every string. The rest become puppets.

npcs.bio: Rules {PLANET}, and is proud of being precisely average at it. Perfectly balanced fleet, standard shields — by design.

npcs.name: Grish

lines.text: Have your explorers found any clues about the 10th Gate?
Not yet. But we track deep-space anomalies on the rim. Some call it the Earth Gate.
A world where our ancestors turned to pure light. I would spend a whole Colony Ship to find it.
Are you ready to back the Player if Luxor attacks?
You bet your tail I am! Grant wants balance. My Fighter hull is already primed.
If Lox starts a fight, {PLANET} flies beside you.

npcs.bio: {PLANET}'s explorer, and the reason its rim survey keeps overrunning. Would spend a whole Colony Ship on a rumour of the tenth gate.

npcs.name: GUNNER

lines.text: Don't just stand there, start shooting these drones!

npcs.bio: Runs the range on {PLANET} Lake and has run it for eleven years. Keeps the drones, keeps the key, and has not missed in front of anybody yet.

npcs.name: Master of Arms

lines.text: They say you train the guard.
I train whoever walks in. You included, if you have the stomach for the circle.
What should I be working on?
Four things, and everyone favours the wrong one. ATTACK is what your blade takes off them. DEFENSE is what you shrug off.
SPEED is the one nobody respects — it is your feet, your reach, and how often a blow finds nothing but air where you were.
SMARTS is what your scanner tells you and what a clever fox can talk their way into. Sharp enough and doors open that never open for a big arm.
And which do YOU favour?
The one my opponent has neglected. Step in the circle and I will tell you which of yours that is.

npcs.bio: Thirty years in the circle. Has never once been the strongest fox in it and has never once lost to the fox who was.

npcs.name: Guard Captain

lines.text: Captain.
Steward. You have the look of someone who has been winning fights and has not yet asked why.
Ask. I have opinions and a desk, which is a dangerous pairing.

topics.label: What makes a good soldier?
replies: Not courage. Courage is cheap at the start of a thing and gone by the middle of it.
Habit. The fox who has done the boring part ten thousand times does it right on the one day it matters, and does not have to be brave about it.
Show me a guard who keeps their kit clean when nobody is watching and I will show you someone who will still be standing at dusk.

topics.label: When should you NOT fight?
replies: Almost always. Every fight you take is one you could have walked round, and walking round costs you nothing but pride.
Pride is the most expensive armour in this building. It weighs nothing and it has killed more of my foxes than crystal ever has.
The golems on the mountain do not want anything. You cannot negotiate with a rock. But most of what you will meet out there is not a rock.

topics.label: How do you beat something bigger than you?
replies: You do not beat it. You outlast the part of it that is trying to beat you.
Anything large is slow somewhere — in the turn, in the recovery, in the moment after it commits. Find that, and then be somewhere else during it.
And do not stand where it is looking. That sounds like a joke. It is most of the craft.

topics.label: What is the worst habit you see?
replies: Watching the weapon. Everyone watches the weapon. The weapon goes where the shoulders have already decided it will go.
Second worst: fighting the last fight. You beat something once and you keep swinging the answer to a question nobody asked again.
Third: finishing tired. If you are still swinging when your arm is done, you are just handing them the ending.

topics.label: Nothing for now, captain.
replies: Then go and be useful. The door is where you left it.

npcs.bio: Commands the barracks. Has thought about fighting for longer than most of the room has been alive, and would rather nobody had to.

npcs.name: Volley

lines.text: You two have been at this a while.
All month. Nobody in here will play me any more.
You have a steady paw. Five goals, and I will not go easy — that is the compliment.

npcs.bio: Has held this table against all comers for a month. Says so, anyway.

npcs.name: Pip

lines.text: Any advice?
Yes. Do not watch the puck, watch their paw — the mallet goes where the paw went first.
Take my end. Five goals. I could do with the rest.

npcs.bio: Loses to Volley about four games in five and turns up anyway.

npcs.name: Sal

lines.text: What's good today?
Everything is good today. The left oven runs hotter, so the left ones are better.
You used to be a bathhouse.
We used to be a lot of things. Now we are hot on the bottom and soft in the middle, which is an improvement.

npcs.greeting: Two minutes on the stone. You want it hot or you want it now?
npcs.bio: Runs the kitchen at the Pizza Place. Two ovens, one pair of hands, and no interest in anybody's opinion about pineapple.

npcs.name: Bramble

lines.text: What's the best thing in here?
Depends. Do you want the one that is good, or the one I will not shut up about?
The second one.
SUPERFOX, issue forty. He gives up the cape for eleven pages. ELEVEN. I had to sit down.
And the robot one?
IRON FOX. All bolts and no feelings, allegedly. Read issue twelve and tell me that with a straight face.

npcs.greeting: Careful of the spinner, it bites. Anything you want, I have read it twice.
npcs.bio: Owns the shop, reads the stock, and has never once sold the last copy of anything he had not finished himself. Built for sitting behind a counter and he knows it.

npcs.name: Pip
npcs.greeting: It is your place, boss. Say the word and I will get the sign painted.
npcs.bio: Front of house. Hands out tokens, wipes down the cabinets, and has been waiting for somebody to tell him what to paint on the sign.

npcs.name: Ross

lines.text: Anything biting?
Always. Whether it comes up is a different question.
What's in there?
Silver perch, mostly. And one old thing down deep that has taken four of my hooks and given nothing back.

npcs.greeting: Quietly, if you would. They can hear you.
npcs.bio: West shore, first light. Has a spot and will not say where.

npcs.name: Brin

lines.text: Good day for it?
Flat water, no wind. Terrible for fishing. Lovely for standing here.
Then why stand here?
Because it is lovely. Keep up.
Heard anything about the mountain?
Snowmen on the pistes and something the size of a barge in the cave. And the lifts are still running. This town.

npcs.greeting: Quietly, if you would. They can hear you.
npcs.bio: East shore. Fishes standing up because sitting down makes her impatient.

npcs.name: Otto

lines.text: Two rods?
One for the fish and one for the look of the thing. Doubles my odds either way.
Caught much?
A boot, a bottle, and something I put straight back without looking at it.

npcs.greeting: Quietly, if you would. They can hear you.
npcs.bio: Works the jetty. Two rods out, neither watched closely.

npcs.name: Mara

lines.text: All the way out here?
The deep shelf drops off right under us. Everything worth catching is under your feet.
Is it safe?
It has held me for nine years. It will hold you for a chat.

npcs.greeting: Quietly, if you would. They can hear you.
npcs.bio: Out on the pontoon, furthest from the shore and the conversation.

npcs.name: Nix

lines.text: There are snowmen out there.
There are. Nobody built them. They were not there at last light and they are there now, and that has been the arrangement for three weeks.
And you still run the lift?
Something odd is going on out in the galaxy, friend. Something odd is always going on out in the galaxy. The chair runs at eight.
That is not reassuring.
It is not meant to be reassuring. It is meant to be open.
What is down the west trench?
A fort. Walls, towers, flags, the lot. Went up in a fortnight and none of us saw a soul do it.
Has anyone been in?
Two went to look. Both came back. Neither has said much since, except that the one on the throne is wearing a crown.

npcs.greeting: Bar comes down, tips come up. And if you see one on the piste, ski round it, not past it.
npcs.bio: Runs the lift. Counts every fox up and every fox down, and the numbers have matched all season.

npcs.name: Perri

lines.text: Is the mountain safe?
No. Is that going to stop anybody? Also no. I have a class of six at ten and all six will be here.
Which ones are dangerous?
The still ones throw. The ones that come at you have icicles for arms. Learn the difference from far away, not near.
Why is this happening?
Ask the church. Ask the sky. I teach snowplough turns.
There is a fort out west.
There is. The rope goes all the way in, which I find the most upsetting part. Somebody roped it. Something roped it.

npcs.greeting: Knees soft, look where you want to go. And where you want to go is not at the ones with the arms.
npcs.bio: Teaches beginners on the flat by the lodge. Endlessly patient, faintly amused.

npcs.name: Bram

lines.text: People still ski with all this going on?
Every day. I have stopped being surprised. I put a shovel by the door and I keep the fire going.
Have you been up to the grotto lately?
Not in a year. Wren and Barrow are still down there, mind. Two of them, that age, in the dark, with those things.
Are they alright?
They were always odd. Odd is fine. But odd and forgetting is different, and somebody ought to go and see. I keep meaning to. I keep not going.

npcs.greeting: Boards on the rack, not in the snow. And do not go up without telling somebody.
npcs.bio: Waxes boards, digs out the racks, keeps the cocoa on. Never actually skis.

npcs.name: Wren

lines.text: There are worms in here the size of a boat.
Wonderful, aren't they. We raised every one. Barrow started the feeding and I never had the heart to stop him.
They attacked me.
They do not know you. They have never had to know anybody. Forty years and only the two of us down here.
You should close the cave.
Close it? We open at nine. We have always opened at nine. What day is it?
Are you alright?
I forget where I have put things. I have not forgotten the worms. Ask Barrow, he is on the boat. He will tell you the same and he will be wrong about the year.

npcs.greeting: Mind the rope. Barrow says they know their own names now, and I have stopped arguing about it.
npcs.bio: Keeps the grotto with her husband Barrow. Between them they have hand-fed the worms since they were the length of a finger, and neither will hear a word against them. Sharp about the cave, hazy about everything else — she asked the town for help twice and was too proud to ask a third time.

npcs.name: Barrow

lines.text: How big do they get?
Big as you feed them, and I have never once given short measure. That is not a boast. I have been thinking about it.
One of them is enormous.
The Fed One. Under the crystal. He was my first. Came out of the wall the same week Wren and I were married.
Does he know you?
He did. He did, definitely. I take the boat over and I put the bucket down and... I do not go over any more. Wren does not know that. Do not tell Wren.
You two need help down here.
We manage. We have always managed. We managed when it was two of us and a lamp, and we will manage now she keeps asking me what day it is twice in a morning.

npcs.greeting: Boat leaves when it is full. Wren counts the tickets. Wren counts everything.
npcs.bio: Rows the grotto boat, and has done since the year he married Wren. Fed the first worm out of his own lunch pail and every worm since. Getting on now, and starting to lose the thread — but he still knows every one of them by the light it carries.

npcs.name: Hope

lines.text: You came all this way?
You built a clubhouse and a pizza place and a comic shop and told us nothing. Of course I came.
How is home?
Fine. Quiet. Which is more than anyone is saying about out here — every planet on the network has something new walking about on it.
You've heard about the mountain?
Snowmen with icicles for arms and a fort with a crown on the throne. And the lifts still running. I like this town.
And the cave?
That is the one I would not laugh at. Two old foxes down there on their own, and something under the crystal that used to fit in a lunch pail. Go and see them properly.

npcs.greeting: There you are. I was starting to think I would have to call.
npcs.bio: Came out to see the place for herself, and has been standing beside the throne since the morning bells asking Grant questions he cannot answer. Wears the eight, same as you.

npcs.name: Noble

lines.text: What are you doing out here?
Watching. It was a tennis court when I last stood here and now there is ice in there and a net at each end. Somebody has been busy.
That was me.
I know it was you. I am telling you I noticed.
Hope is at the castle.
She is asking the King about the sky. She has been asking everybody about the sky. She is not wrong to.
Is something happening out there?
Something is always happening out there. What is new is that it has started arriving. Keep the eight where people can see it.

npcs.greeting: Four a side and not one of them looked at the clock. Beautiful.
npcs.bio: Stands outside the stadium with his paws behind his back, watching foxes knock each other over and enjoying it more than he will admit. Wears the eight because he always has.

npcs.name: Furlong

lines.text: Do you run games here?
I drop the puck. Whether it is hockey or eight foxes falling over is between them and the boards.

npcs.bio: Drops the puck on this ice and has never once been argued with about an offside. Keeps the whistle, the watch and the opinions.

npcs.name: Fleet

lines.text: You always get there first.
Somebody has to. Whether I am still holding it a second later is a separate question and I would rather not take it now.

npcs.bio: First to every puck on this ice and goes over if you breathe on her. Has been told about it and does not intend to do anything about it.

npcs.name: Cinder

lines.text: Do you ever change it up?
No. That is the whole of it. Everyone else changes around me and calls it tactics.

npcs.bio: Does the same thing every shift whatever anybody else is doing, which looks like a lack of imagination until about the third period.

npcs.name: Bracken

lines.text: You leave it very late.
I leave it exactly as late as it needs. There is no prize for being first into the corner.

npcs.bio: Slow to the puck, and once she is there nobody takes it off her. Shoots from her own blue line and the goalie hears about it for a week.

npcs.name: Quill

lines.text: What is this place?
The Relic Museum of {PLANET}. Two rooms, ten cases, and one exhibit, which is me standing in it.

npcs.greeting: Careful of the spinner, it bites. Anything you want, I have read it twice.
npcs.bio: Curates the second comic shop, which is now ten glass cases and a fox with a label printer. Has never left this square and does not intend to.

npcs.name: Plum

lines.text: Busy today?
Every day, near enough. The library reshelves on a Thirdday and the whole avenue queues for it.

npcs.bio: Walks the north avenue most days. Has opinions about the state of the paving.

npcs.name: Mauve

lines.text: Anything I should know?
Mind the crossing. Everyone cuts the corner at the crest and nobody looks.

npcs.bio: Crosses the square four times a day and could not tell you why.

npcs.name: Iris

lines.text: Good morning.
It is, actually. The lilac took at last — third year of trying.

npcs.bio: Grew the lilac in half the window boxes on this street.

npcs.name: Brother Cinnabar

lines.text: Are you of the church?
Of the order, yes. We are not only for the nave. Somebody has to see the town.

npcs.bio: Acolyte of the Church of {PLANET}. Past the novitiate. Trusted with a shrine of their own.

npcs.name: Amethyst

lines.text: Waiting for something?
A crate. Due on the last ship, and the last ship has been and gone.

npcs.bio: Waiting on a delivery that was due on the last ship.

npcs.name: Lilac

lines.text: You know everyone here.
By their walk, mostly. Faces change. Nobody changes how they cross a square.

npcs.bio: Knows every fox on the square by their walk before their face.

npcs.name: Sister Damson

lines.text: You are a long way from the church.
Sent out to look at it. Hard to pray for a town you have only seen from a window.

npcs.bio: Novice of the Church of {PLANET}. Newly of the order. Still gets the early bells.

npcs.name: Orchid

lines.text: Keeping well?
Between jobs. Have been for a year. It suits me better than the jobs did.

npcs.bio: Between jobs, cheerfully, for about a year now.

lines.text: Welcome to Home, Steward.
Your ship is fuelled and berthed behind you. The teleporter at the end of the gantry puts you down on the crest pad in town.

topics.label: How do I get back to space?
replies: Walk back to your ship and board her. She will take you up to orbit.
